lastText: File ClosedThe Price of the PolicyContestedAllied Combined Chiefs, 1940 — 1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) — filed late, out of sequenceImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945 — slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign reaches its end having spent more Western Allied lives than the historical record — the price of the bolder, more aggressive road at several of this campaign's genuine forks. The Strait of Messina was sealed rather than left to the Patton–Montgomery race — denying Kesselring's Italian defense some of the roughly 100,000 veteran troops it historically escaped with. Stalin was pressed hard on Poland's postwar government at Yalta rather than accepted on ambiguous terms — a harder line taken exactly where the historical conference chose accommodation. Force Z sailed against the Japanese landings without fighter cover and was sunk on December 10, 1941, with some 840 men: the first capital ships sunk at sea by aircraft alone. Germany's defeat was never a variable Western Allied command decisions controlled, only its timing, its cost, and the shape of the peace that followed it.One Year LaterA year past victory in Europe, the machinery of occupation is running on the arrangements this campaign's own conferences — Tehran, Yalta, the ones this command actually attended — settled or failed to settle in advance.
